open_items.detail: The source says the Speaker of the House of Assembly was appointed by the Governor from members or non-members. The 1954 Order in Council appointed the federal House of Representatives Speaker from outside its membership; regional arrangements differed by region, with some Speakers appointed and others elected.
open_items.required_action: In GOV-LES-T2-W06-CORRECTED-WEEK, distinguish the federal House of Representatives from the regional Houses and identify the appointment/election procedure for each region from the 1954 Order and amendments. Do not generalize one regional arrangement to all Houses.

open_items.detail: The source says the constitution introduced direct elections into federal and regional legislatures throughout Nigeria. The 1954 Order allowed election regulations to provide for direct or indirect elections and different methods in different parts of Nigeria; Northern representation continued to involve indirect electoral colleges.
open_items.required_action: In the corrected supplement, distinguish direct elections in some regions from indirect arrangements in the North. Cite the 1954 Order's election provisions and avoid claiming a uniform electoral system.

open_items.detail: The source says the Governor-General 'continued to be the Executive Council'. Under the 1954 constitutional arrangements, the Governor-General chaired/presided over the Federal Executive Council; he was not the Council itself. The constitution did not yet create a Nigerian Prime Minister at the centre.
open_items.required_action: Correct the institutional description: distinguish the Governor-General from the Federal Executive Council and explain the continued colonial executive role and ministerial arrangements. Do not describe the Governor-General as the Council.

open_items.detail: The source says the 1954 revenue formula worked on derivation instead of need and national interest. The fiscal arrangements were more complex: derivation was important, particularly for mineral rents/royalties and personal income tax, but earlier and subsequent arrangements also used need, population, national interest and other criteria.
open_items.required_action: In the corrected supplement, identify the relevant Chick Commission and constitutional-era fiscal arrangements, distinguish the derivation principle from the full revenue formula, and cite the specific allocation report. Do not state that need and national interest were wholly absent.

open_items.detail: The source states that the regional structure encouraged regionalism, ethnicity and national disunity. Regional institutions did strengthen regional political identities, but the claim is an interpretation and cannot be presented as the sole or automatic cause of national disunity.
open_items.required_action: In the corrected supplement, explain both the federal accommodation of regional diversity and the political tensions associated with regional competition. Attribute interpretations and avoid a single-cause explanation.

open_items.detail: The 1958 resumed Constitutional Conference met at Lancaster House, London, from 29 September to 27 October 1958. It considered minority concerns, regional self-government, fiscal matters and independence. The Willink Commission recommended safeguards for minorities but did not recommend creating new regions before independence; the conference fixed independence for 1 October 1960.
open_items.required_action: In the corrected supplement, distinguish proposals and questions considered from decisions reached. State the London venue and exact dates, explain the minority safeguards, note that no new regions were created before independence, and include the agreed independence date.

open_items.detail: The scheme entry says 'Lagos conference of 1958', while the assigned source says the 1958 Constitutional Conference was held in London from 29 September to 27 October 1958. The official resumed conference report confirms Lancaster House, London. A separate 1954 constitutional conference was held in Lagos.
open_items.required_action: Preserve the scheme wording and the source's London locator separately. Do not silently change the scheme to London; obtain owner/teacher confirmation before editing the scheme text. The historical note may explain that 1954 and 1958 conferences had different venues.
